learning_outcomes.text: Explains fundamental elements regarding the composition of atmospheric air.
Defines the main measurable properties for fluids that transport energy in thermal systems.
Interprets and represents processes on the humid air diagram.
Describes the functioning of ventilation and air conditioning systems.
Describes constructive and functional elements of specific equipment (fans, chillers, air handling units).
Uses calculation methods for air flows, thermal powers, and cooling/heating loads.
Sizes ducts and ventilation channels.
Knows norms and technical regulations regarding indoor air quality.
Integrates air conditioning systems with other building systems.
Has notions of operation, maintenance, and fault diagnosis.
Analyzes and interprets psychrometric diagrams to determine air parameters.
Sizes ventilation ducts and air conditioning equipment.
Utilizes calculation and modeling software for air conditioning and ventilation processes.
Chooses technical solutions appropriate to the type of building and its destination.
Interprets functional and technological schemes of installations.
Correlates air conditioning installations with other technical systems of the building.
Calculates and sizes the main elements in ventilation and air conditioning installations.
Makes independent technical decisions in usual design and operation situations.
Respects technical standards and norms in the proposed solutions.
Addresses elements related to indoor air quality and user comfort with responsibility.
Is autonomous in utilizing software tools and measurement equipment.
Is capable of arguing and supporting technical solutions before beneficiaries.
Manages material and energy resources efficiently.

syllabus_topics: Elements of humid air thermodynamics
Air calculation parameters for air conditioning installations
Requirements for ventilation
Ventilation and air conditioning systems
"All-air" type air conditioning
"Air-water" type air conditioning
Refrigerant-based air conditioning
Component elements of air conditioning and conditioning installations: Fans
Component elements of air conditioning and conditioning installations: Heating and cooling coils
Component elements of air conditioning and conditioning installations: Dust filters
Component elements of air conditioning and conditioning installations: Humidification chambers
Component elements of air conditioning and conditioning installations: Heat recuperators
Presentation and use of main methods for measuring air parameters
Disassembly and assembly of different types of fan coil units
Disassembly and identification of elements of an air handling unit
Simulation of defects on an air handling unit
Measurement of speed, flow rate, and sound pressure level for a fan coil unit
Maintenance and periodic inspection of fan coil units
Determination of flow rate and available pressure for an air handling unit
Working with the humid air diagram. Simple transformations in the psychrometric diagram
Simple processes with humid air
Complex air treatment in winter. Calculation and sizing of heating coils and humidification equipment
Complex air treatment in summer. Calculation and sizing of cooling coils and dehumidification equipment
Calculation and sizing of heat recuperators in air handling units
Calculation and sizing of filters in air handling units
Calculation and sizing of auxiliary equipment in air handling units. Mixing chambers, droplet separators, dampers and shut-off valves, etc.
teaching_methods: Description of physical and mathematical models
assessment_rules: A minimum grade of 5 is required for each of the discipline's activities (exam, laboratory). The final evaluation result is obtained by considering the scores and weights allocated to each activity within the discipline. Grades will be awarded from 1 to 10, with grade 5 certifying the acquisition of minimal learning outcomes and the awarding of corresponding study credits.
